title: Hidden circle revealed
line: x²+y²−6x+4y−12=0 regroups into two completed squares, and a circle with center (3,−2) and radius 5 draws itself.

title: Expanding hides the move
line: The circle x²+y²=25 slides to center (3,−2) while its equation expands term by term, burying the center inside −6x and +4y.

title: Two squares, one ellipse
line: 4x²+9y²−16x+18y−11=0 completes two squares and divides by 36, then an ellipse centered at (2,−1) appears with axes 3 and 2.

title: Completing an actual square
line: x²+6x becomes an x-by-x square plus a 6-wide strip that splits in half, wraps two sides, and leaves a 3×3 corner to fill.

title: Solving with the filled square
line: For x²+6x=16, adding the 3×3 corner makes area 25, so the side x+3 is 5 or −5, landing on x=2 and x=−8.

title: Sliding into vertex form
line: y=x² slides right 2 and down 3 and lands exactly on y=x²−4x+1 as that equation rewrites itself as (x−2)²−3.

title: The vertex walks a path
line: As b slides from −6 to 6 in y=x²+bx+2, the vertex moves along its own upside-down parabola while h=−b/2 counts beside it.

title: Counting sign flips
line: In x⁵−x⁴+3x³+9x²−x+5 an arrow hops over each sign change, counting 4, so there are 4, 2, or 0 positive roots.

title: Shadows of a graph
line: Light shines down on y=√(x−2)+1, casting its shadow on the x-axis as the domain, then sideways onto the y-axis as the range.

title: Fold for even, spin for odd
line: y=x²−3 folds along the y-axis onto itself, y=x³−x spins half a turn onto itself, and y=x³+1 fails both tests.

title: A zero peels off a factor
line: The cubic x³−2x²−5x+6 hits zero at x=1, so (x−1) splits off, and the leftover quadratic's graph shows the other zeros −2 and 3.

title: Shrinking the candidate list
line: All twelve Rational Roots candidates for 2x³−3x²−11x+6 line up on a number line, the graph drops in, and only −2, 1/2, and 3 survive.

title: Peeling a quartic down
line: Each root of a quartic divides out, and the graph redraws as the quotient drops from degree 4 to 3 to 2.

title: Factor pairs that add up
line: The factor pairs of 12 roll past with their sums 13, 8, 7, and 3 and 4 light up to drop into (x+3)(x+4).

title: Tiles into a rectangle
line: One x² square, seven x-strips and twelve unit squares shuffle around until they form a perfect (x+3) by (x+4) rectangle.

title: From crossings to an equation
line: Dots at x=−2 and x=5 turn into factors (x+2)(x−5), multiply into x²−3x−10, and a parabola threads both dots, then stretches by 2.

title: Function machine f
line: Numbers 1, 2, 3 drop into a box labeled f(x)=2x+3, come out as 5, 7, 9, and fly to their spots on a graph.

title: Vertical line sweep
line: A vertical line sweeps across y=x² hitting it once each time, then across x=y² where it hits twice and flashes red.

title: Arrows from inputs
line: An arrow diagram links inputs to outputs; when one input sprouts a second arrow, the relation stops being a function.

title: Adding k lifts the graph
line: As k counts from −3 to 3, y=x²+k rides up and down the plane without changing shape.

title: Why minus moves right
line: For y=(x−3)², each table row's point slides 3 to the right, because the input now has to be 3 bigger to give the same output.

title: Steering a square root
line: y=√x moves step by step to y=√(x+2)−1 while its starting point leaves a trail from (0,0) to (−2,−1).

title: The 1-3-5 staircase
line: From the vertex of y=x², steps of over 1 and up 1, 3, 5 build both arms; for y=2x² the steps become 2, 6, 10.

title: T-chart to parabola
line: Rows of a T-chart for y=x²−2x−3 fill in one by one, each point flies onto the plane, and a curve joins them through the turn.

title: Where the shadings overlap
line: y≥x−2, y<−2x+4 and x≥0 each shade a half-plane in a different color until only the triangle where all three overlap stays lit.

title: Arms reaching from 3
line: For |x−3|<2, arms of length 2 reach out from 3 and light up 1 to 5; flip to > and two outer rays light instead.

title: Above the axis wins
line: The parabola y=x²−x−6 crosses at −2 and 3, the parts above the axis glow and drop onto a number line as two rays.

title: Sliding the profit line
line: Over a polygon of feasible points, the line 3x+2y=P slides outward until it touches only one corner, the best answer.

title: Why corners win
line: A dot walks along an edge of the feasible region while P=3x+2y counts steadily up, so the best value must sit at an endpoint.

title: Halving toward a root
line: x³−x−1 changes sign between 1 and 2; the interval halves again and again while the camera zooms and digits of 1.3247 lock in.

title: Stacking graphs to add
line: Vertical sticks from the axis up to y=x² and y=x stack end to end, and their tops trace out the graph of y=x²+x.

title: Piecewise in pieces
line: Three formulas draw faintly across the whole plane, then each gets trimmed to its own interval with open and closed dots at the seams.

title: Zoom out to the ends
line: y=x³−4x²+x+6 wiggles near the origin, but as the camera zooms out it becomes nearly identical to plain y=x³.

title: Four ways the arms point
line: Flipping the leading sign and switching between even and odd degree swings a polynomial's two end arrows into all four up/down patterns.

title: The fraction factory
line: Factors of 6 and of 2 pair up into every fraction p/q, duplicates merge, and the list settles onto a number line of candidate roots.

title: Remainder equals height
line: Dividing x³−2x+5 by x−2 leaves remainder 9, and on the graph the point above x=2 rises to height 9 as well.

title: Formula meets the crossings
line: For y=x²−2x−3, −b/2a marks the axis of symmetry, then ±√(b²−4ac)/2a steps 2 each way and lands on −1 and 3.

title: The discriminant decides
line: As c rises in x²+2x+c the parabola lifts, the discriminant 4−4c counts down through zero, and crossings go from 2 to 1 to 0.

title: Coefficients into slots
line: The colored a, b, c of 2x²+3x−5 fly into matching slots of the formula and simplify to 1 and −5/2.

title: Deriving the formula with a square
line: ax²+bx+c=0 divides by a, the x-square grows two b/2a strips, the missing corner fills, and the steps morph into the quadratic formula.

title: Roots from the vertex
line: A parabola written as a(x−h)²+k crosses at h±√(−k/a); swapping in h and k from b and c turns that into the formula.

title: Sigma as a counter
line: As i ticks from 1 to 5 in the sum of 2i−1, each term pops out as an L of dots, nesting into a 5×5 square.

title: Either factor can be zero
line: Lines y=x−2 and y=x+5 multiply into a parabola, and wherever either line hits zero the parabola hits zero too.

title: Line meets circle
line: The line y=x+k slides across the circle x²+y²=25, and the intersection count drops from 2 to 1 at tangency to 0.

title: Cutting a square from a square
line: A small b-square is cut from an a-square, the L-shape's strip swings around, and it becomes an (a+b) by (a−b) rectangle.

title: Flipping over the x-axis
line: Each point (a, b) of the sideways parabola x=y²−4 walks straight across the x-axis to (a, −b) and lands back on the curve.

title: Bring down, multiply, add
line: Dividing x³+2x²−5x−6 by x+3, coefficients drop, multiply by −3, and add down the row until the remainder 0 glows.

title: Double x, see what y does
line: x doubles on both y=2x and y=12/x; on the line y doubles, on the hyperbola y halves, shown by growing and shrinking bars.

title: Racing toward x=2
line: A dot on y=1/(x−2) creeps toward x=2 from both sides while its y readout dives toward −∞ and shoots toward +∞.

title: (a+b)² as an area
line: An (a+b)-sided square splits into a², two ab rectangles and b², and the 1, 2, 1 coefficients appear as the pieces are counted.

title: Pascal feeds the expansion
line: Pascal's triangle builds by adding pairs, then row 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 drops into (a+b)⁴ as a's powers fall and b's rise.

title: Picking a or b four times
line: All 16 ways to pick a or b from four brackets, like abab, sort into piles of sizes 1, 4, 6, 4, 1.

title: Unstacking a fraction
line: Top and bottom of a stacked fraction get multiplied by the common denominator 6x, and the little denominators cancel away visibly.

title: Powers of i go around
line: Multiplying by i turns a point a quarter turn each time, carrying it from 1 to i to −1 to −i and back to 1.

title: Adding complex numbers as arrows
line: 3+2i and 1−4i become arrows on the plane, tip meets tail, and the sum 4−2i is where the second arrow ends.

title: Through two machines
line: x=1 follows arrows through the point set g to 3, then through f to 7; another input gets stuck where f has no match.

title: Slicing the cone
line: In a side view of a double cone, a cutting line tilts and the slice beside it turns from circle to ellipse to parabola to hyperbola.

title: Which conic from the signs
line: Sliders change A and C in Ax²+Cy²=1, and the graph morphs from circle to ellipse to hyperbola as their signs and sizes change.

title: Same distance to both
line: A point moves so its distance to the focus (0,1) and to the line y=−1 always match, and its trail draws a parabola.

title: Dish to focus
line: Vertical rays fall into a parabola, bounce off its wall, and every one of them passes through the focus.

title: Pythagoras draws a circle
line: A point circles (2,1) at distance 5 while its right triangle's legs x−2 and y−1 change length and their squares always sum to 25.

title: String and two pins
line: A pencil point moves with distances to foci (±3,0) changing, but their sum stays 10, tracing out an ellipse.

title: Whispering gallery
line: Rays leave one focus of an ellipse in every direction, bounce off the curve, and all meet at the other focus.

title: Constant difference
line: A point keeps its distances to foci (±5,0) differing by exactly 6, and both branches of a hyperbola appear as it moves.

title: Hugging the asymptotes
line: For x²/9−y²/16=1, a 6-by-8 box's diagonals extend into asymptotes, and as the camera zooms out the branches cling to them.

title: Cramer's rule as areas
line: The column vectors of a 2×2 system form a parallelogram; swapping one column for the answer column makes another, and x is their area ratio.

title: Determinant as area
line: Columns (3,1) and (1,2) span a parallelogram of area 5; as one column turns parallel to the other, the area shrinks to 0.

title: Criss-cross diagonals
line: Arrows draw down one diagonal of a 2×2 and up the other, then a 3×3 copies its first two columns for six diagonal products.

title: Adding versus doubling
line: Two bars grow side by side, one adding 2 each step and one doubling from 1, until the doubling bar shoots off screen.

title: Doubling every five steps
line: On y=3·2^(x/5), every 5 units right the height doubles, from 3 to 6 to 12 to 24, marked by bracket after bracket.

title: Turning the base dial
line: As b slides from 0.5 to 3 in y=b^x, the curve pivots through (0,1), going flat at b=1 and flipping from decay to growth.

title: Swapping exponents into logs
line: Points like (3,8) on y=2^x swap to (8,3), crossing the line y=x, and together draw y=log₂x.

title: Doubling to climb one
line: On y=log₂x, marks at x=1, 2, 4, 8, 16 rise by exactly one each, so each equal step up needs twice the distance right.

title: Sketching from clues
line: For y=(x+1)/(x−2), intercepts appear as dots, asymptotes x=2 and y=1 dash in, test points land, and two curve pieces get drawn.

title: Adding one more column
line: A staircase of k(k+1)/2 dots gains a column of k+1 dots, and the formula morphs into (k+1)(k+2)/2 to match.

title: Dominoes that must fall
line: A first domino labeled n=1 falls, and each domino k is shown knocking over k+1, so the whole endless row goes down.

title: Sign chart from factors
line: (x+2), (x−1) and (x−4) each get a sign row that flips at its zero, the product row fills in, and the graph above confirms it.

title: Holes and zeros split the line
line: For (x−3)/(x+1)≤0, the line splits at an open hole at −1 and a closed dot at 3, and test points light up the middle interval.

title: Swapping across y=x
line: Points (1,2), (2,4), (3,4) swap their coordinates and fly across y=x; two land above x=4, so the inverse fails the vertical line test.

title: Log counts the multiplying
line: For log₂32, 2 multiplies by itself while a counter ticks 1 to 5 until it reaches 32, so the log is the count.

title: Stretching a ruler into a log scale
line: Points 1, 10, 100, 1000 slide from an ordinary number line to equal spacing, each step meaning one more power of ten.

title: A slide rule multiplies
line: Two log-scale rulers slide so 1 sits over 2, and 6 appears under 3, because adding lengths log 2 and log 3 makes log 6.

title: Power rule by stacking
line: log(m³) unfolds into log(m·m·m), three copies of a log m bar stack end to end, and they become 3·log m.

title: Change of base is a stretch
line: The graph of log₁₀x stretches vertically by about 3.32 and lands exactly on log₂x.

title: From system to grid
line: In a system of three equations, the variables and plus signs fade, and the coefficients slide together into a bracketed grid.

title: Adding moves a triangle
line: A triangle's vertex coordinates sit in a matrix; adding a matrix of 2s and 1s shifts every vertex, and the triangle slides together.

title: Row meets column
line: A row slides across a column, matching entries multiply and pop out, and their sum drops into one spot of the product.

title: A matrix bends the plane
line: A grid shears under the matrix [[1,1],[0,1]]; the arrows for x and y land on the matrix's columns while grid lines stay parallel.

title: Scalars stretch the shape
line: Multiplying a triangle's coordinate matrix by 3 pushes every vertex three times farther from the origin.

title: Order matters
line: A square is rotated then sheared, and a copy is sheared then rotated; the two end up as different shapes, so AB≠BA.

title: Row moves, same answer
line: Each row operation on a 2×2 system redraws its two lines: scaling leaves a line alone, adding rows swings one line around the fixed intersection.

title: Undoing a matrix
line: A square turns into a parallelogram under [[2,1],[1,1]], then its inverse matrix pulls it back to the exact same square.

title: Cross out and shrink
line: For each entry in the top row of a 3×3, its row and column get crossed out, the leftover 2×2 slides out, and signs alternate.

title: Difference pyramid
line: Under 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 the differences 3, 5, 7, 9 appear, then 2, 2, 2, and the pyramid builds back up to 36.

title: Two curves add to one
line: The graphs of 1/(x−1) and −1/(x+1) add point by point and land exactly on the graph of 2/(x²−1).

title: Cancel factors, not terms
line: The x's in (x+2)/(x+5) get wrongly crossed out, then plugging in x=1 gives 3/6 against 2/5, and the mistake flashes red.

title: Matching the bases
line: 4^(x+1)=8^x rewrites as 2^(2x+2)=2^(3x), the 2s fall away, and the graphs of both sides cross at x=2.

title: Unwrapping a log
line: log₂(x+3)=5 flips into 2⁵=x+3, and the curve y=log₂(x+3) meets the line y=5 at x=29.

title: The answer that isn't
line: Solving x/(x−2)=2/(x−2)+3 gives x=2, but the graphs show both sides blow up there, so the curves never actually meet.

title: Two lines, three outcomes
line: One line turns against a fixed line: they cross at one point, slide apart as parallels with none, then merge with infinitely many.

title: Tuning a sine wave
line: Starting from y=sin x, A stretches it to height 3, B squeezes the period to π, C shifts it, D lifts it.

title: Depression equals elevation
line: From a cliff, the angle looking down at a boat and the boat's angle looking up are shown to be alternate angles of equal size.

title: Ratios ignore size
line: A right triangle with a 35° angle grows and shrinks, its sides changing, while opposite over hypotenuse stays stuck at 0.574.

title: Whose opposite is it
line: The reference angle hops between the two acute corners of a right triangle, and the opposite and adjacent labels swap places.

title: sin 15° from 45 and 30
line: Angles of 45° and 30° on a unit circle leave a 15° gap, and sin(45°−30°)=(√6−√2)/4 matches the height of that point.

title: Finding the angle from sides
line: A ray swings up from 0° and stops when its rise over run reaches 5/12, reading off the angle 22.6°.

title: Work one side only
line: The left side tan x·cos x morphs step by step into sin x while the right side never moves, then their graphs overlap exactly.

title: Four triangles rearranged
line: Four 3-4-5 triangles slide around inside a 7×7 square, first leaving a tilted 5×5 hole, then a 3×3 and a 4×4 hole.

title: Counting tiles
line: The 9 unit tiles on side 3 and the 16 on side 4 fly over and fill the 25-tile square on the hypotenuse.

title: Triangles in every quadrant
line: A ray at 150° drops a line to the x-axis, making a 30° reference triangle with negative x; then 210° and 330° follow.

title: Wrapping the radius
line: A radius peels off, bends around the circle, and fits a bit over 6 times, so a half turn is π radians or 180°.

title: How tall is the flagpole
line: From 20 m away at a 35° sight angle, a right triangle draws itself and 20×tan 35° counts up to a 14 m flagpole.

title: A slice of the whole
line: As a sector's angle sweeps to 360°, its area and arc length count up in step, ending at πr² and 2πr.

title: Every solution of sin x = 1/2
line: The line y=1/2 cuts a sine wave at π/6 and 5π/6, then again every 2π, matching two points on a unit circle beside it.

title: Half a square, half a triangle
line: A unit square splits along its diagonal into a 1-1-√2 triangle, and an equilateral triangle of side 2 splits into 1, √3, 2.

title: The square-root staircase
line: A point climbs a unit circle at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° while its height reads √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2.

title: Unrolling the circle
line: A point spins around a unit circle while its height is carried to the right, tracing out a sine wave one turn at a time.

title: Cosine is a shifted sine
line: The x-coordinate of a spinning point traces a cosine wave, which then slides right by π/2 and lands on the sine wave.

title: Squares on sine and cosine
line: As a point moves around a unit circle, squares drawn on its sine and cosine legs change size but their areas always total 1.

title: Building sin(A+B)
line: Two right triangles stack with angles A and B, and the top corner's height splits into sin A cos B plus cos A sin B.

title: Coordinates are cos and sin
line: A point rides a unit circle while dashed lines drop to each axis, reading cos θ and sin θ as their signs change by quadrant.

title: Tangent on the circle
line: A ray from the center hits the line x=1 at height tan θ, which shoots up toward infinity as θ nears 90°.

title: Filling in the special points
line: The first quadrant's 30°, 45° and 60° points reflect across both axes, filling the circle with all sixteen special coordinates.
